title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results 'Stationarity is necessary and sufficient to drive vibrations in males'; Fig. 3C-D; Fig. S4C; Table 1
quote: Conversely, inducing female walking by optogenetically activating the DNp28 neurons55,56 nearly abolished vibrations (Fig. 3C, D).
mapping_basis: Paper names the neuron DNp28 but the driver is SS01587 (R11H10-p65.AD; VT033947-GAL4.DBD, Table 1), which driver_lines.csv maps to DNp29 (Namiki 2018 Supp file 3; Supp Table 5 eLife.107450); the line identity was preferred over the printed name, so confidence is medium.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 89 mW/cm2, 5 s on / 25 s off, 30 trials
sensory_condition: female courted by a wild-type male in a 44 mm chamber on paper over microphones; room light off
penetrance: female velocity rose from about 1 mm/s to about 10-12 mm/s during light (Fig. 3C mean trace)
n_flies_note: DNp28-Chrimson+ N = 9 pairs; controls DNp28-Gal4+ N = 4, UAS-Chrimson+ N = 5, DNp28-Chrimson- N = 7
notes: Locomotion measured as body velocity from video tracking (no leg tracking); coded as walking for all legs per the 'increased locomotion' convention, so confidence medium. Name/line conflict: paper says DNp28 but SS01587 is listed as DNp29 in the kit.

title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results 'Central song neurons drive song and vibration with complex dynamics'; Fig. 4B; Table 1
quote: The activation of the descending neurons pIP10 or pMP2 drove song but no vibrations.
mapping_basis: pIP10 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 14 mW/cm2 in order, 5 s on / 115 s off, 15 trials
sensory_condition: solitary male in 44 mm chamber, room light off
penetrance: all pIP10-Chrimson males sang (Fig. 4B fraction responded = 1); no vibration
notes: Genotype UAS(FRT.STOP)CsChrimson; VT40556-GAL4/fru-FLP. Only song/vibration scored; legs and locomotion not described for this line. The paper also contains its own circuit model (not a Pugliese-type screen).

title: Cellular and functional dissection of the octopaminergic and tyraminergic system in the Drosophila brain.
source_locator: Results 'ASM4/5 neurons acutely suppress aggression', para 2; Fig. 6B (image not available locally)
quote: Optogenetic activation of VL neurons and ASM1–3 neurons did not decrease aggression relative to genetic controls except OTA-SG05 (Figure 6B).
mapping_basis: The paper's VL cluster comprises descending subtypes VL1 and VL2 (Results 'Heterogeneity in OA/TA descending neurons'); OA-VL1 is a listed synonym of DNd02 (synonyms.csv); which VL subtype(s) the tested lines label is not stated in the text, hence medium.
stimulation: 655 nm red light, 10 ms pulses at 5 Hz, intensity 12μM/cm2 (as printed)
sensory_condition: pairs of socially isolated males in aggression arena with food substrate, infrared illumination
penetrance: lunge rate not decreased relative to genetic controls
n_flies_note: number of pairs printed only in Fig. 6B, which was not available locally
notes: Readout is aggression (JAABA lunge counts), not legs; walking speed (Fig. 6D) was reported only for ASM lines OTA-SG08/SG10/SG40. Driver line IDs for the VL lines and n are in Fig. 6B, whose image was not downloaded; the text says new lines target both VL1 and VL2 and ASM1 lines also co-label VL neurons. Marked multi_dn on that basis; a session with Fig. 6B should confirm line IDs and specificity.
